subject: psychology
title: Multi-Store Model: Evaluation & Case Studies
welcome_lead: HM, KF and a model that needed an update.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology MSM evaluation: case studies HM KF, WMM challenge, strengths.
final_note: Strong starting model, but too simple for real STM.

concepts.def: Patient Henry Molaison — hippocampal damage 1953, no new episodic LTM.
Shallice & Warrington 1970 — STM damage but spared LTM.
Musician with viral encephalitis — STM intact, LTM impaired.
MSM supported by case studies showing dissociation between STM and LTM.
STM not unitary — WMM offers a richer model.
MSM remains a foundational scaffold despite its simplicity.

walkthroughs.body_html: HM (1953) had bilateral hippocampectomy for epilepsy. He could not form new episodic LTM but kept STM (digit span normal) and procedural memory (mirror-drawing improved without recall). Supports MSM's STM-LTM split. Studied by Milner until his death in 2008.

KF (Shallice & Warrington 1970) had verbal STM digit span of only 2 after a motorbike accident, yet LTM was intact. Challenges MSM's claim that LTM is filled via STM — if STM is impaired, how is LTM normal? Supports WMM's multi-component STM.

Strengths: clear, falsifiable, predicts capacity/duration/encoding differences, supported by case studies. Weaknesses: too simple, ignores LTM subtypes (Tulving), ignores elaborative rehearsal (Craik & Lockhart 1972), treats STM as unitary. Still — a foundational model.

mcqs.q: HM's surgery in 1953 removed which structure?
KF's case argues against which MSM assumption?

numericals.q: In what year did HM have the surgery that destroyed his ability to form new memories?

free_texts.q: What process did Craik & Lockhart 1972 propose as superior to maintenance rehearsal?
